candidates.title: [Bug]: XML template with a mismatched end tag is accepted
candidates.body: ### Description An XML template expression whose end tag does not match its start tag compiles and evaluates to a well-formed element, silently dropping the bad end tag. `xml:fromString("")` correctly returns an error for the same text. ### Steps to Reproduce ```ballerina import ballerina/io; public function main() { xml x = xml ``; // @error io:println(x); } ``` Run with `go run ./cli/cmd run repro.bal`. Actual: ``` ``` Expected: ``` a compile-time error: end tag does not match start tag ``` ### Spec reasoning Spec §6.6.2 (XML template expression): "The result of the previous step is parsed as XML content. More precisely, it is parsed using the production content in the W3C XML Recommendation." The parse and conversion to an xml value happen statically; the evaluation step only inserts interpolated values, so a template that is not well-formed has no meaning and must be a compile-time error. XML 1.0 §3, WFC Element Type Match: "The Name in an element's end-tag MUST match the element type in the start-tag." XML 1.0 §5.1: "Violations of well-formedness constraints are fatal errors." The prefixed form `xml ``` is accepted the same way. ### Affected Version(s) main @ ea2bcd439 ### OS, DB, other environment details and versions Linux (cloud container), interpreter built from source with `go run ./cli/cmd run` ### Related area Parser ### Related issue(s) (optional) None found.

candidates.title: [Bug]: duplicate attribute in an XML template is accepted and the last value wins
candidates.body:
### Description

An XML template expression with the same attribute twice compiles, and the last value silently wins. When one of the values is interpolated (`xml `<a b="${s}" b="2"/>``), it is instead a runtime panic (`duplicate XML attribute "b"`). Two prefixes bound to the same namespace URI (`<a p:x="1" q:x="2" xmlns:p="u" xmlns:q="u"/>`) are also accepted. `xml:fromString("<a b='1' b='2'/>")` correctly returns an error.

### Steps to Reproduce

```ballerina
import ballerina/io;

public function main() {
    xml x = xml `<a b="1" b="2"/>`; // @error
    io:println(x);
}
```

Run with `go run ./cli/cmd run repro.bal`.

Actual:
```
<a b="2"/>
```

Expected:
```
a compile-time error: duplicate attribute b
```

### Spec reasoning

Spec §6.6.2 parses the template with the XML `content` production, before evaluation. XML 1.0 §3.1, WFC Unique Att Spec: "An attribute name MUST NOT appear more than once in the same start-tag or empty-element tag." Namespaces in XML 1.0 §6.3 also forbids two attributes with the same expanded name. Well-formedness violations are fatal errors (XML 1.0 §5.1), so this must be reported at compile time rather than resolved silently (or by a runtime panic in the interpolated case).

### Affected Version(s)

main @ ea2bcd439

### OS, DB, other environment details and versions

Linux (cloud container), interpreter built from source with `go run ./cli/cmd run`

### Related area

Parser

### Related issue(s) (optional)

None found.

candidates.title: [Bug]: predefined `xml` prefix rejected in XML templates (`xml:lang`)
candidates.body:
### Description

Using the predefined `xml` namespace prefix in an XML template (e.g. `xml:lang`) fails with `undefined XML namespace prefix 'xml'`. `xml:fromString("<a xml:lang=\"en\"/>")` and `createElement("a", {[xmllib:lang]: "en"})` both work and give the expected value. Since `xml` is a reserved word, the prefix cannot be declared with an ordinary `xmlns` declaration either.

### Steps to Reproduce

```ballerina
import ballerina/io;
import ballerina/lang.'xml as xmllib;

public function main() {
    xmllib:Element e = xml `<a xml:lang="en"/>`;
    io:println(e.getAttributes()); // @output {"{http://www.w3.org/XML/1998/namespace}lang":"en"}
    io:println(e); // @output <a xml:lang="en"/>
}
```

Run with `go run ./cli/cmd run repro.bal`.

Actual:
```
error[SEMANTIC_ERROR]: undefined XML namespace prefix 'xml'
 --> repro.bal:5:32
```

Expected:
```
{"{http://www.w3.org/XML/1998/namespace}lang":"en"}
<a xml:lang="en"/>
```

### Spec reasoning

Spec §6.6.2 parses the template as XML content and turns it into an XML Infoset. Namespaces in XML 1.0 §3: "The prefix xml is by definition bound to the namespace name http://www.w3.org/XML/1998/namespace. It MAY, but need not, be declared". XML Infoset §2.2 [in-scope namespaces]: "This set always includes the namespace with prefix xml".

The Ballerina spec's XML namespace section also treats `xml` as implicit: "There will be a synthesized namespace attribute for every prefix other than xml", and on serialization "If the namespace name is http://www.w3.org/XML/1998/namespace, then use a prefix of xml". lang.xml defines `lang` as `"{http://www.w3.org/XML/1998/namespace}lang"`.

Related: when the prefix is forced through `xmlns "http://www.w3.org/XML/1998/namespace" as 'xml;`, the attribute map also gets a synthesized `{http://www.w3.org/2000/xmlns/}xml` entry, which the "other than xml" rule above forbids.

### Affected Version(s)

main @ ea2bcd439

### OS, DB, other environment details and versions

Linux (cloud container), interpreter built from source with `go run ./cli/cmd run`

### Related area

Semantics

### Related issue(s) (optional)

#1226 (template namespace handling rejects `xmlns=""`) is a sibling problem in the same code.

candidates.title: [Bug]: XML attribute values are not whitespace-normalized (tab/newline kept)
candidates.body:
### Description

A literal tab (or newline) inside an attribute value is kept as-is instead of becoming a space, as XML attribute-value normalization requires. This happens both in XML templates and in `xml:fromString` (`xml:fromString("<a c=\"p\tq\nr\"/>")` gives `p\tq\nr` instead of `p q r`).

### Steps to Reproduce

```ballerina
import ballerina/io;
import ballerina/lang.'xml as xmllib;

public function main() {
    // NOTE: the attribute value below contains a literal TAB character between p and q
    xmllib:Element e = xml `<a c="p	q"/>`;
    io:println(e.getAttributes()); // @output {"c":"p q"}
}
```

Run with `go run ./cli/cmd run repro.bal`.

Actual:
```
{"c":"p\tq"}
```

Expected:
```
{"c":"p q"}
```

### Spec reasoning

XML 1.0 §3.3.3 Attribute-Value Normalization: "For a white space character (#x20, #xD, #xA, #x9), append a space character (#x20) to the normalized value." (a character reference such as `	` is appended as the referenced character, i.e. stays a tab).

Spec §6.6.2 says the template is parsed as XML into an Infoset, and "interpolated expressions may occur as Character Information Item or in the [normalized value] of an Attribute Information Item". The XML namespace section builds the attributes map with an entry for each attribute information item, whose value is its [normalized value] (XML Infoset §2.3). Ballerina's own source newline normalization does not touch TAB, so the literal tab reaches the XML parser. Values inserted through `${...}` interpolation come after parsing and should not be normalized.

### Affected Version(s)

main @ ea2bcd439

### OS, DB, other environment details and versions

Linux (cloud container), interpreter built from source with `go run ./cli/cmd run`

### Related area

Runtime

### Related issue(s) (optional)

#1091 (entity/char references not decoded in template text and attribute values) is related but covers a different rule.

notes:
Spec fetched OK (ballerina.io/spec/lang/master). Stopped at the 5-candidate limit after about 35 minutes.

Dropped as duplicates of existing issues:
- Ranges: #1454 (range used as a value crashes), #1169 (int:MAX inclusive range overflows), #1349 (byte binding over a range).
- Operators: #1046 (unary -/~ keep the subtype), #1262 (no singleton typing for shift/bitwise), #1217 (compound assignment evaluates lvexpr first).
- Queries: #1047 (join right side re-evaluated), #1149 (readonly expected type), #1129 (limit scope).
- Equality explorer: #1091 (xml template entity refs), #1133 (closures compare ===), #1215 (method value crash).
- start on a never-returning call assigned to future<int> is rejected. #1071 covers it; the maintainer closed it saying the never special-casing is intentional, so it was dropped.

Confirmed but not included (over the 5 cap). Both were checked as new and validated from the spec:
- decimal:floor/ceiling of a value with a positive exponent returns a value whose coefficient exceeds 34 digits. `(1E+40d).floor()` prints a 41-digit integer; `(1E+6000d).floor()` prints 6001 digits. Repro: decimal x = 1E+40d; io:println(x.floor()); expected 1E+40 (IEEE roundToIntegral) or at least a valid decimal. Violates §5.2.4.2 (coefficient fits in 34 digits). Related: #1403, #1347.

Found by explorers but not deduplicated or validated (good seeds for the next run):
- Client resource method with an unnamed path param (`resource function get a/[string]/[int n]()`) panics at runtime with 'too many arguments'. Unnamed rest param `[int...]` too. Spec §5.6.3.5 makes param-name optional.
- Quoted resource method name in an access (`c->/z.'default`) is not unquoted: compile error 'no matching resource method'. Related #1116.
- Identifier escapes in resource path segments are not unescaped (`resource function get a\-b()` is unreachable via `c->/["a-b"]`; the rest param gets `x\.y`; service attach point gets `a\-b`). Related #1351, #1116.
- NaN bit patterns are not canonicalized: float:NaN.toBitsInt(), fromBitsInt(-1).toBitsInt() and fromString("NaN").toBitsInt() all differ, but the langlib doc says all NaN bit patterns map to a single NaN value. This conflicts with corpus subset9/09-langlibs/float1-v.bal:93, so it may be intentional.
- isolated class field initializers are not checked for isolation: `private int[] xs = shared;` with a mutable module var is accepted and leaks it (§6.8.1.1).
- readonly class fields are not typed as T & readonly (`readonly class C { int[] xs = [1]; }` lets you push to xs). This may overlap with #1043.
- XML well-formedness gaps not filed: `]]>` in template text, PI target `xml`, `xmlns:xml`/`xmlns:xmlns` redeclaration accepted. A forced `xmlns ... as 'xml` adds a synthesized xmlns:xml attribute.
